components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 1rem; border: 1px solid rgba(168, 66, 34, 0.2); background: #a84222; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(17, 19, 20, 0.05); transition: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #6c2b11; transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(17, 19, 20, 0.12); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(168, 66, 34, 0.45); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Bikash Chicken Point is designed to feel like a clean, dependable local butcher counter on warm cream paper—direct, readable, and built for quick mobile decisions at home or in the market. Its color system draws from Sanzo Wada's A Dictionary of Color Combinations (wada-sanzo-colors.com), pairing earthy Brick Red, Deep Brown, Yellow Ocher, Ivory Buff, and Ecru over sunlit parchment surfaces.

The visual hierarchy prioritizes fast scanning: shop identity, live counter status, phone/WhatsApp actions, and cut availability come first, followed by clear step-by-step pre-booking and counter QR tools. Tactile press feedback (scale(0.97)), custom exponential easing, and concentric corner radii give every interactive control a grounded, physical feel.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper canvas with an ambient Brick Red top wash and crisp 1px Ecru-derived borders
High-contrast Wada Black and Warm Brown ink for effortless mobile daylight readability
Sturdy geometric display headings paired with humanist body copy, tabular monospace rates, and light Bengali accents
Tactile, grounded controls with subtle press-down feedback and mathematical concentric corner geometry

rules.name: The WhatsApp Green Rule
rules.body: Reserve whatsapp-green strictly for WhatsApp links/buttons, UPI verification cues, and live open-counter status—never use it as a generic brand accent.

rules.name: The Wada Warmth Rule
rules.body: Keep all neutrals in the Wada Sanzo warm paper-to-brown-black family (canvas-cream, ivory-buff, ecru, brown-warm, wada-black); never introduce cold slate grays.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Always apply tabular-nums and the monospace stack to counter rates, weights, and rupee totals so numbers align cleanly across cards and ledgers.

rules.name: The Grounded Card Rule
rules.body: Reserve hover-lift elevation exclusively for genuinely clickable surfaces; static KPI and product summary cards remain flatly grounded at rest.

rules.name: The Concentric Nesting Rule
rules.body: Any inner container nested inside a padded panel or control must step down its border radius (outer radius - padding) using --radius-concentric-panel or --radius-concentric-control rather than repeating the outer radius.

dos: Do use Button, Chip, Surface, and ModalSheet primitives instead of ad-hoc <button> or <div> styles.
Do gate hover transforms behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and pair pressable controls with active:scale-97 and --ease-out-expo.
Do use tabular-nums and monospace styling for all prices (₹/kg), weights, and PhonePe UTRs.
Do step down nested border radii using --radius-concentric-panel and --radius-concentric-control.
donts: Don't use transition: all; always specify exact composited/color properties (transform, background-color, border-color, box-shadow).
Don't apply hover-lift to non-clickable KPI or product summary cards.
Don't use whatsapp-green for non-WhatsApp / non-open-status decoration.
Don't use font-size < 16px on mobile <select> or <input> controls where iOS Safari auto-zoom can trigger.
